title: Mapping methodologies: Exploring visual narratives of identities, families, and power with immigrant‐origin and marginalized youth
abstract: Abstract Mapping methodologies offer a versatile and innovative approach to understanding the complexity of youth identities, families, and communities, while also attending to the systems of power, privilege, and marginality in which they are embedded. Mapping involves participant‐generated drawings that are integrated into broader qualitative interview protocols, amplifying youth voices in the process. Participants are given colored pencils, paper, and an open‐ended prompt inviting them to depict their identities, families, and/or communities. These “visual narratives” serve as entry points for deeper qualitative inquiries into topics that are often multifaceted, sensitive, and especially salient for individuals at the intersections of multiple marginalities. This methodological paper presents mapping as a qualitative research tool and offers a practical guide for planning, implementing, and analyzing maps with diverse adolescent and emerging adult populations.
